year.label: 2004 Morgan Aero 8 N-GT / GTN race specification

records.real_world_identity_notes: The PMR telemetry name Aero 8 GT(N) resolves to the 2004 Morgan Aero 8 N-GT/GTN race specification, not the limited-production road-going Aero 8 GTN special edition and not the later Aero 8 GT3. PMR explicitly labels its implementation a 2004 Aero 8 N-GT. Period RSC records identify the Morgan Works Race Team chassis SA9AERO89000490272 in 2004 competition. The race car used a six-speed sequential gearbox, while the 2002 race documentation separately records a physical AP four-disc carbon clutch. No reviewed source establishes the exact driver interface, clutch procedure, shift electronics, or real race-period wheel geometry.
records.confidence_basis: PMR's official page and dated article identify the 2004 Morgan Aero 8 N-GT/Aero 8 GTN. Racing Sports Cars independently records the exact 2004 Morgan Works Race Team Aero 8 GTN chassis SA9AERO89000490272. Contemporary Morgan material identifies the GT(N) as a race car entering the 2002 Le Mans and British GT program, and Autosport reports the race version's Getrag six-speed sequential-shift transaxle. The repository contains no existing curated record for this identity, so a new record is proposed.

records.specification_basis: PMR and its 2004 article state six-speed sequential, Autosport reports the race Getrag six-speed sequential transaxle, and the exact 2002 race-car technical table lists six ratios. The official PMR 2004 description and contemporary Autosport race-technical report both explicitly identify a sequential race gearbox. The race gearbox is explicitly described as sequential-shift. This establishes the sequential pattern, but not the driver's physical actuation interface. Manual blip is a downshift action in this controls model; no upshift-blip claim is asserted. Automatic blip is a downshift action in this controls model; no upshift-blip claim is asserted. Throttle lift is represented as an upshift action in this controls model; no separate downshift-lift claim is asserted. Automatic cut is represented as an upshift action in this controls model; no downshift-cut claim is asserted. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/shift_actuation, /authentic_controls/transmission/standing_start_clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/manual_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_blip, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shape, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/open_top, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/integrated_display, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shift_lights.
